messages.subject: Average confidence intervals after ranef?
parts:
This is maybe more a stats question than a modeling question, but I have not been able to find an answer - maybe someone here has experience with this.

I have created an abundance model using pcountOpen, with a number of sites within an area. After creating the model, I also applied Bayesian inference using ranef(). 
This is a model that runs over a number of years (primary periods) and I want to show the trend over time for the whole area (not the separate sites).

So after ranef I get get the abundance and CIs for all my sites, and to summarize for the area overall, I am reporting the mean abundance. My question is about the CIs: can I also average these?

I first considered summing but already figured I can't sum sum the CIs like I can sum the abundance - and my models are too large for bootstrapping (this was suggested in another post). 
Giving the mean would be a good alternative (also because I have actually created a number of models for a number of areas that have different sizes; using the means makes it easier to compare). My only question is whether I can also average the CIs - and if not, what alternatives there are to get the CIs?

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Average confidence intervals after ranef?
parts:
Hi Geraldine,

You shouldn't average the confidence intervals. Instead, you need to compute the (empirical Bayes) posterior predictive distribution. I can show you how to do that if you send along a short and sweet reproducible example of the problem. 

Eventually, I'd like to add general functionality for doing posterior prediction after running ranef(). 

Richard

Thanks Richard, I'll try to get a bit of a shorter version of the data/model uploaded.
FYI, what I do now is the standard textbook / manual calcs:

re <- ranef(final_model)
N_hat_sites <- bup(re, stat = "mean", na.rm=TRUE)
# sites in rows, years in columns
colMeans(N_hat_sites) # average abundance for each year over the whole area

# confidence intervals
confint(re, level=0.95) # these are the ones that I have to average somehow for the whole area.

I noticed by the way that bup() and confint() give me the same means and CIs as the ones that are already produced as part of ranef(); but I guess these functions make it easier to work with the result? (since they're not S4 objects like re?)

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Average confidence intervals after ranef?
parts:
I created an example based on the simulation in the help page for pcountOpen. This draws a bunch of posterior samples from the posterior predictive distribution of total abundance in each year. Let me know if you have any questions.


library(unmarked)

example(pcountOpen)

re1 <- ranef(m1)

plot(re1, layout=c(5,5),

     subset=(year==1)&(site<26),

     as.table=TRUE)



## Draw posterior samples of annual abundance

## You could modify this to compute any function of the posterior

postPredN <- function(ranefOut, nSims=100) {

    post <- ranefOut@post

    postDim <- dim(post)

    nSites <- postDim[1]

    nProbs <- postDim[2]

    possibleN <- 0:(nProbs-1)

    nYears <- postDim[3]

    NsitePostSamples <- array(NA_integer_,

                              c(nSites, nYears, nSims))

    for(i in 1:nSites) {

        for(t in 1:nYears) {

            NsitePostSamples[i,t,] <- sample(

                possibleN, size=nSims,

                replace=TRUE, prob=post[i,,t])

        }

    }

    NpostSamples <- apply(NsitePostSamples, c(2,3), sum)

    return(NpostSamples)

}



Npost <- postPredN(re1, nSims=1000)

 rowMeans(Npost)             ## Posterior mean of annual abundance

apply(Npost, 1, median)     ## Posterior median

apply(Npost, 1, quantile,

      prob=c(0.025, 0.975)) ## 95% CI

 colSums(N)              ## Actual values (see help page example)
